correctness.rationale: At the specified marked trapezoid the closure Jacobian in the last two angles has determinant sin(pi/3), so the chart is smooth and locally covers all nearby shapes with the given marking. The chain remains simple near the reference, and the only turn whose sign can change is delta. Differentiating closure gives last-angle increments delta-alpha and alpha. The five varying diagonal distances have aggregate first variation h*delta, with h=sqrt(3)/2 and S(0)=9+2sqrt(3). An interior direction between edge normals cannot minimize the positive width, since the support pair is fixed and the width has second derivative minus itself. The two oblique edge-normal families have reference width 2h and drop out. For the other three, direct support projection gives width increments (delta+|delta-alpha|)/2, (delta+|alpha|)/2, and delta/2+max(0,-alpha,alpha-delta). Their minimum is max(delta,alpha,delta-alpha)/2 at first order, including chamber boundaries. Taylor errors remain uniformly quadratic under the finite minima and maxima. Division gives the claimed first variation; comparing the loss with delta+|alpha| in the three chambers gives equality of the linear bound only at alpha=delta>0. That ray stays in the strictly convex domain and proves sharpness. This proves a local result, not the unrestricted global inequality.
residual_risks: The angular sharp coefficient depends on the specified coordinates. No claim is made about finite-distance or global stability.

value.rationale: For the distance/width extremal problem, the symmetric calculation leaves open asymmetric directions of improvement at the proposed optimizer. The result rules out all such nearby directions, identifies the three competing support families and gives the worst local loss in the declared coordinates. That is useful local information about the conjecture without pretending to prove the global bound.
